As the primary subject matter expert, you will serve as the trusted advisor for project managers and gatekeepers on all process inquiries.The role works through influence across a matrixed, multi-cultural organisation and is a service to colleagues rather than an audit function. R&D is in active transformation on tooling and data quality, so ambiguity and shifting priorities are part of the job.Your Responsibilities:- Drive continuous optimisation of the global Stage-Gate Work Packages, ensuring deliverables are lean, consistent and harmonised across brands and regions.- Maintain and enforce the global R&D governance framework: processes, tools, RASCI models, cadence structures and compliance checkpoints.- Safeguard gate readiness, documentation integrity and audit readiness across all gate transitions.- Define, track and report R&D KPIs covering gate discipline, cycle time and pipeline health.- Develop and maintain digitalized templates, blueprints, work instructions and process documentation that simplify execution for project managers.- Coordinate cross-functional and cross-regional alignment, so local delivery conforms to global R&D standards.- Ensure Stage-Gate documentation and gate data are captured consistently and kept current in the governing systems, and represent process requirements towards the system owners.- Build and maintain the R&D Knowledge Hub as the single, topic-structured source for process documentation, templates and training material, curated as an ongoing exercise.- Ensure data continuity between Stage-Gate governance and Product Lifecycle Management (PLM), acting as the business-side representative to translate process requirements into system specifications with the Global PLM team.Your Profile:- Bachelor's or Master's degree in Engineering, Business Management, Industrial Management or comparable.- 7 to 10 years in process management, R&D project management or operational excellence, gained across more than one industry, ideally in product development or manufacturing.- Proven implementation of Stage-Gate or comparable phase-gate models- Working understanding of project and portfolio management systems used in an R&D environment (e.g. Planisware Orchestra, SAP) and good data literacy for KPI definition and process analysis.- Interest in how AI, automation and digital tools can simplify product development processes.- Solid understanding of PLM, ERP, and engineering change management systems (e.g., SAP, Planisware Orchestra), with the ability to align process governance with system architecture.- Demonstrated comfort, curiosity and respect across cultures and working styles is a core requirement.- Gives and receives feedback constructively.- Lean, Six Sigma or comparable optimisation approaches an advantage.- Strong moderation and stakeholder skills, able to steer cross-regional teams without direct reporting lines. Able to translate between technical detail and business framing.- Business-fluent English required, German an advantage.Our offer:- A salary package that ties directly to your work experience and responsibilities- Comprehensive health management, including an on-site fitness room, local and digital health services, Health Cashback, and Hansefit membership- Diversity & Inclusion: We offer equal opportunities for all individuals and support your personal development- Access to a wide range of employee benefits, such as discounts on travel, fashion, media, mobile phones, and more- A highly motivated, appreciative, and international team that inspires you and offers opportunities to learn and grow- A modern company restaurant to ensure your well-being during the dayInterested?Then we are looking forward to your application!

jobs.occupation: Research Scientist and Curator (m/f/d)  of the section Vertebrata (Tenure Track) (Biologe/Biologin)
jobs.description: Senckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN), headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position at the Senckenberg Museum of Natural History in Görlitz, ideally as of April 1, 2027:Research Scientist and Curator (m/f/d) of the section Vertebrata (Tenure Track)(full time / part time options available)Location: GörlitzEmployment scope: full time / part time options are availableType of contract: initially limited to three years;the type of time limitation depends on individual profile and legal framework (maximum 3+3 years). A permanent employment is planned after a positive evaluationRemuneration: collective agreement of the German Länder, TV-L E13The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.The renowned Senckenberg Museum of Natural History, located in the medieval town of Görlitz, combines research at an international level with extensive collections and an engaging museum programme. The surrounding Upper Lusatia region offers a large variety of opportunities for experiencing nature.Senckenberg is committed to study the causes and effects of biodiversity loss in the Anthropocene. As part of our strategic development, we launched an ambitious long-term research effort in “Anthropocene Biodiversity Loss” encompassing the modules “Collectomics”, “Biodiversity Genomics”, and “Solution Labs”. Objectives include the transformation of natural history collections into the digital era, studying biodiversity from the genome to the ecosystem levels and offering exploratory spaces for science and society to develop common solutions to Anthropocene challenges.For the Görlitz vertebrate collection, which comprises approximately 70,000 specimens (preserved using dry, cryogenic, and liquid preservation methods, with the focus on mammals; birds make up a smaller proportion, while other vertebrate groups represent only a small fraction), we are seeking an internationally recognized scientist with a solid track record in mammal research, possibly supplemented by work on another vertebrate groups.Potential research topics may include various aspects such as mammalian diversity, functional morphology, phylogeny, or biological interactions. Curation and collection-based research should play a significant role in the applicant’s research approach. The selected candidate should be open to research collaborations with SGN colleaguesYour tasks- Scientific curation and development of the vertebrate collection and the associated resources as an important international research infrastructure through international networking, growth, and improved accessibility.- Develop a visible portfolio of collection-based research with basic and applied aspects in the broad field of mammalogy and possibly other vertebrate groups by using a range of established and innovative methods and approaches.- Taking responsibility for the relocation of the collection items, including the infrastructure of the Mammalogy/Vertebrate Section, to the new campus at Bahnhofstraße 30 at Görlitz.- Secure external research funds.- Publish results of your research in international scientific outlets.- Establish collaborations with ongoing projects, regional and national (region (e.g., long-term projects on wolf, lynx) and international (e.g., Africa, Mongolia), including with other sections and departments in Görlitz and further Senckenberg institutes.- Communicate with external stakeholders such as scientific associations, conservation agencies, local and regional authorities, as well as citizen scientists.- Participate in teaching in the MSc level programmes of International Institute Zittau/ Dresden University of Technology.Your profile- Doctoral degree in biology/zoology or a related field- Expert knowledge of mammals, including native species (the biogeographic focus of the mammal collection is currently the Palearctic), additional expertise in other vertebrate groups- Proactive willingness to implement innovative research approaches, such as in the field of genomics, morphometrics, AI, imaging, 3D methods, pollutant analysis in a collection context- Ability to identify attractive research questions and make use of synergies through collaborations- Excellent academic track record adequate to your career stage- Experience in the acquisition of third-party funding and project management- Experience in supervising staff (doctoral candidates, BSc., MSc., students, technical staff), ability to work in a team- Very good command of German (B2)- Fluency in English, both spoken and written- Class B driving licence (international driving licence)- Willingness to travel on occasion to the extent possible considering your personal circumstancesDesirable skills- Knowledge in molecular, biochemical or biophysical techniques in taxonomy and ecology- Knowledge in research data management and databases- Experience in curation and management of zoological collections, and in museum workWe offer- Access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations- An attractive job within the inspiring and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution with excellent infrastructures and collaborations opportunities, e. g. in morphology, genomics, evolutionary biology, (paleo-)ecology- A working place in completely new building with dissection and other laboratories, collection rooms, in the historic town of Görlitz with rapidly developing local research community (DZA, CASUS, IHI/TUD, HiLusatia), yet situated very close to nature with high mammal diversity and opportunities for field work- Opportunities to participate in teaching and outreach activities, e.g., in our museum and with collaborating universities- Opportunities for establishing an independent academic working group and acquiring further academic qualifications- Flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement – company pension planSenckenberg is committed to diversity. We benefit from the different expertise, perspectives and personalities of our staff and welcome every application from qualified candidates, irrespective of age, gender, ethnic or cultural origin, religion and ideology, sexual orientation and identity or disability. Women are particularly encouraged to apply as they are underrepresented in the field of this position; in the case of equal qualifications and suitability, they will be given preference. Applicants with a severe disability will be given special consideration in case of equal suitability. Senckenberg actively supports the compatibility of work and family and places great emphasis on an equal and inclusive work culture.How to apply?Please upload your application (letter of motivation with a short description of your previous and current research foci, a CV, certificates of academic achievements, list of publications as well as letter(s) of recommendation, if available) as a single PDF file by November 10, 2026.https://www.senckenberg.de/de/stellenanzeigen/For data protection information on the processing of personal data as part of the application and selection process, please refer to the privacy policy on our homepage at https://www.senckenberg.de/en/imprint/For further information about the Senckenberg Gesellschaft für Naturforschung please visit www.senckenberg.deContactSenckenberg Gesellschaft für NaturforschungSenckenberganlage 2560325 Frankfurt a.M.For specific questions about this role please contact Prof. Dr. Hjalmar S. Kühl.E-Mail hjalmar.kuehl@senckenberg.de

A focus of our research are Engineered Living Materials (ELMs), an emergent class of materials from the combination of inert materials and living organism, with huge potential for sustainable innovation in different technological fields. Across the institute, materials scientists, synthetic biologists and biophysicists cooperate to understand living and inert matter, and to realize new materials with unprecedented functions from a synergistic interfacing.We are strongly linked to collaborative initiatives in the ELM field including the Leibniz ScienceCampus LifeMat, Living Therapeutic Materials, the Priority Program SPP2451 “Living Materials with Adaptive Functions”, and the MaterialVital Hub.As part of our ELM research community, we are seeking aPostdoctoral Researcher with expertise in Microbial Biophysics (f/m/d)with interest in the fundamental understanding of microbial communities within synthetic microenvironments. The candidate will be part of an interdisciplinary research team within the Department Dynamic Biomaterials at INM.Your roles:- Experimental research to understand microbial behaviour in confined spaces (synthetic hydrogels) and dynamic environments using imaging, microfluidics and molecular biology methods.- Scientific cooperation with researchers in materials science and synthetic biology at INM, and with external partners in bioanalytics/bioinformatics within running funded projects.- Compilation and presentation of research results in the form of progress reports and presentations at project meetings and scientific conferences.- Communication of research results within the scientific community at conferences and scientific events, and publication in scientific journals.- Co-supervision of students and doctoral researchers.- Support and promote the digitalization of ELM research in collaboration with dedicated experts in the group.Your profile:- PhD degree in biophysics/cell biology or related discipline.- Experience during your PhD or previous postdoctoral stay as experimental researcher in the field of microbial biophysics.- Interest in collaborative and interdisciplinary research challenges.- Self-driven and hands-on personality. Organization and prioritization skills.- Very good communication skills in English.We offer:- Work in an emergent research topic, with multiple opportunities to develop a competitive research profile.- An interdisciplinary research environment with complementary expertise and ready to share knowledge and support your work.- State-of-the-art infrastructure, including access to Core Facilities run by experts.- Access to a broad international network with vibrant scientific collaborators and exciting cooperation projects.- A highly professional and supportive working environment with an open and international culture.- A well-structured on-boarding process and clear responsibilities.- Transparent opportunities for career development.- Flexible working hours and mobile working opportunity.- A family-friendly working place.- A EG 13 TV-L position (full time). A part time position is also possible.The position is initially for 2 years.Interested?We look forward to your application! Please upload your CV and motivation letter, by October 15th, 2026 via the online application system. For further information on this position, please contact INM Scientific Director and Head of the Research Department Dynamic Biomaterials Prof. Dr. Aránzazu del Campo (aranzazu.delcampo@leibniz-inm.de ).The INM practices an open and appreciative corporate culture in which the existing diversity is promoted and lived. The institute is an equal opportunity employer with a certified family-friendly policy, and it provides offers for a better work-life balance, flextime, and mobile working. We promote professional opportunities for women and strongly encourage them to apply. Full time jobs can be generally divided. People with disabilities are expressly encouraged to apply and will be given priority if equally qualified.

on AWS, including compute, storage,databases, messaging, security, and monitoring- Strong experience with PostgreSQL, SQL, data modelling, and Entity Framework Core- Practical experience with Infrastructure as Code, CI/CD, containers, automated testing, observability, andproduction operations- Ability to work across the full application stack, from backend services and integrations to Blazor-baseduser interfaces- Ability to evaluate and adopt new cloud services, frameworks, development tools, and architecturalapproaches where they provide clear technical or business value- Strong practical experience with AI-assisted software development and coding agents, including AI-supported quality and delivery workflows- Strong problem-solving, communication, and technical ownership, with the ability to work proactivelywith customers, product stakeholders, and other engineering disciplines- Proficiency in both English and German (German at least B1)Nice to Have:- Experience with The University Hospital Essen offers first class medical services in the Ruhr metropolis. Every year, 225.000 patients are treated in 30 clinics, 27 institutes and specialized centers. The over 8.000 employees offer medical care with state-of-the-art diagnosis and therapies, which meet highest international standards. Patient care is connected with basic and translational research at an internationally competitive level.Hemoglobin is best known for its role in oxygen transport in red blood cells. Our preliminary findings indicate that it is also expressed by lung immune cells, where it may contribute to antiviral defense. These findings further suggest that the thrombospondin-1 (TSP-1)/CD47 signaling axis limits hemoglobin expression and its associated antiviral antivity.The project aims to uncover the molecular mechanisms underlying hemoglobin-mediated antiviral defense and determine how this response is regulated by TSP-1/CD47 signaling. Combining mechanistic studies with in vivo models, we will explore whether targeting this pathway can enhance antiviral immunity while avoiding excessive inflammation and lung tissue damage.At the Insitute of Medical Microbiology (working group of PD Dr. Torben Knuschke), we are therefore offering the following position, which is fully funded by the German Research Foundation (DFG) and will start on 1 January 2027Perform in vitro and in vivo experiments to characterize the intrinsic and extrinsic (paracrine) funtions of hemoglobin in lung immune and epithelial cellsApply molecular biology techniquesPlan, perform, and analyze therapeutic intervention studiesPresent research findings at national and international conferences and contribute to peer-reviewed publicationsAssist in supervising Bachelors/Masters studentsA completed Master´s degree (or equivalent) in Biology, Molecular Medicine, Immunology, Biochemistry, or a related fieldSolid background in cell culture and standard molecular biology techniquesExperience in laboratory animal science (FELASA B) is an advantageStrong interest in basic research in Virology/ImmunologyIndependent, structured, and team-oriented working-styleExcellent written and spoken English skills; German language skills are a plus but not requiredAn exciting, methodologically diverse PhD project in an internationally visible research fieldDedicated supervision of the doctoral project within a cooperative working group with regular seminarsState-of-the-art laboratory infrastructure at University Hospital EssenInterdisciplinary work with colleagues from other departmentsEnrollment into the Graduate School for Biomedical Sciences BIOME (https://www.uni-due.de/biome)Salary according to the German public sector pay scale (TV-L, E13, 65%), fixed-term for 3 yearsA collegial working environment that encourages independent scientific ideasFamily-friendly corporate culture
